title: Canary & Shadow Validation Playbook — Post-Failure Action Plan
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: A recent canary rollout for the convolutional-embedding model variant resulted in elevated hallucination regressions and a delayed auto-rollback due to missing combined gating rules. This ticket captures concrete follow-ups: a prescriptive playbook for validating canaries using both A/B analysis and shadow traffic fidelity checks, a set of automated safety gates that must pass before traffic ramp, and a short-term patch to ensure faster, observable rollback behavior. The goal is to make future rollouts deterministic and testable end-to-end so developers can trust automated rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope: runbook updates, automated metric gating, shadow traffic integrity tests (ShadowSanity), synthetic A/B evaluation harness, rollback latency instrumentation, dashboarding, and small infra changes to ensure a fail-closed rollback behavior across regions. This does not include large model architecture changes or customer migration plans.
steps_taken: 2026-02-27 09:12 UTC: Canary rollout started to 5% traffic for model-embed-v2-experimental (owner: S. Kapoor)
2026-02-27 10:05 UTC: Spike in hallucination rate on user prompts containing long-context system instructions observed in grafana panel (alert threshold breached)
2026-02-27 10:07 UTC: Automated A/B comparator reported semantic drift vs baseline across 12/20 held prompts (engineer: D. Alvarez)
2026-02-27 10:09 UTC: Auto-rollback did not trigger because combined gating rule (latency+quality) was mis-scoped to OR instead of AND; rollback scheduled manually at 10:15 UTC (oncall: A. Mehta)
2026-02-27 10:30 UTC: Canary rolled back; customers reported intermittent degraded responses for ~18 minutes during ramp and rollback window
2026-02-27 11:00 UTC: Incident call and initial containment; created incident ticket INC-2026-0227 and assigned postmortem lead (M. Chen)
acceptance_criteria: Runbook updated with a prescriptive checklist for canary gating and rollback play (owner: M. Chen)
Shadow traffic fidelity test (ShadowSanity) implemented and run daily in staging with >= 99% request/response parity sampling (owner: E. Park)
Automated combined gating rule (quality AND latency AND error-rate) deployed and exercised in a non-production rollout (owner: D. Alvarez)
Rollback path reworked so full rollback completes within 90 seconds and emits structured events to the console and incident channels (owner: S. Kapoor)
A/B evaluation harness added to runtime CI that can reproduce the top-20 regression prompts before any canary traffic ramp (owner: R. Singh)
follow_up_actions: Update canary playbook: add explicit ordering (smoke -> metric gates -> A/B -> shadow parity -> ramp) and checklist items for SRE/owner handoff. Due 2026-03-12 (owner: Maya Chen)

Implement ShadowSanity: lightweight service that replays a sampled shadow request set and verifies parity on routing, tokenization, and structured outputs. Add alerts for >1% divergence. Due 2026-03-18 (owner: Elena Park)

Fix gating logic: convert existing OR-combined gating to an AND-based policy with tunable thresholds stored in config-store and visible in Console. Add unit tests and a staging rollout. Due 2026-03-14 (owner: Diego Alvarez)

Rollback hardening: add preflight dry-run, ensure caches are cleared deterministically, and add explicit 'rollback-started' and 'rollback-complete' events to tracing. Due 2026-03-16 (owner: Sameer Kapoor)

Create A/B regression harness: a repeatable CI job that runs candidate vs baseline on representative prompt set and outputs a regression report with top delta examples. Due 2026-03-22 (owner: Rohan Singh)

Dashboarding: create a per-canary dashboard in Console showing net hallucination delta, latencies p95/p99, error-rate, and user-visible degradations with links to rollback traces. Due 2026-03-13 (owner: DataViz team)
Oncall drill: run a simulated canary-failure drill using the updated runbook and ShadowSanity in staging, measure time-to-rollback and communication latency. Schedule for 2026-03-25 (owner: SRE)
Postmortem writeup: finalize and link to consolidated learnings and ticket items in Confluence. Due 2026-03-11 (owner: Maya Chen)
notes: Key lesson: shadow traffic is only useful if parity checks validate that traffic shape and tokenization match production; divergence led to under-detection of regressions in the canary variant.
We observed that prefix/KV cache interactions can make short canary ramps misleading; synthetic long-context prompts must be part of any canary smoke set.
Risk: Dedicated/private customers may hide regressions if telemetry sampling is lower; the runbook recommends enabling higher sampling for early ramp phases for these customers.
Operational improvement: surface combined gating policy (AND semantics) in Console so PMs and SREs can preview what would have triggered a rollback before a rollout begins.
